findings.issue: The new guard can leave a shipment unable to move. Once a sibling claim holds the shipping, a shipment whose cancel is FAILED can neither ship (409) nor drop its claim. The only way out is to retry the cancel, and every retry sends the card leg on route PAYMENT_SOURCE. If payment-service keeps declining that refund (for example the card account is closed), the shipment stays in PACKED or earlier with no way forward. An outside party cannot cause this, because only payment-service decides FAILED, so this is a liveness and operations gap, not an exploitable denial of service. It is the same class of problem as the stuck REQUESTED state that the runbook already covers.
findings.fix: Put this state in the runbook (FAILED claim + sibling with cancel_shipping_refund > 0 + attempt rising). Later, add an admin-only way to finish such a cancel through the wallet (refundTo=WALLET, route PAYMENT_WALLET) under the next -r<n> key.

summary: Round 3 of PR-A at 0727afe, reviewed against the r3 delta. The new check in Order.advanceShipment closes a real over-refund. Before it, a sibling could freeze the shipping fee as the completing claim while this shipment was REQUESTED and counted as covered. This shipment could then go to FAILED and be shipped: the customer would get the goods and still keep the shipping fee refunded through the sibling. The check covers sibling claims in REQUESTED and DONE (holdsCancelClaim leaves out FAILED), and only for a FAILED shipment; REQUESTED was already refused. It runs before dropFailedCancel, which is the only place a FAILED claim is dropped. Order.advance with a single shipment, and the admin and seller status routes, all reach this point under the order row lock, so I found no way around it. If the cancel is retried instead, reclaim does attempt++ and freezes the claim again. The shipment then counts the sibling as covered and gets the remainder (its own share), with shipping already taken (0), so the total stays exact. Without shipping, the leftover exposure is at most rounding cents. The check is a read-only test that answers 409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT and moves no money. Only shipments that already have a FAILED claim on an order that is partly being cancelled are affected, and nobody outside payment-service can produce a FAILED, so there is no denial-of-service against fulfilment. The one minor is the stuck state when a card refund keeps being declined, which needs a runbook entry or later an admin wallet fallback. The delta adds no new endpoint, input, log field or dependency. My earlier minors are still on the backlog: the settlement watch for PENDING card refunds, merging A together with B, and the seller's free-text reason in the customer timeline.
